bga_name: La Famiglia: The Great Mafia War
rules_text:
Rules summary Contents 1 Game Overview 2 Game Flow 2.1 1. Planning Phase 2.2 2. Execution Phase 3 Scoring 4 Variants and Options Game Overview In this team-based strategy game , two teams (each consisting of two families) fight for dominance over Sicily during the Great Mafia War of the 1980s. You must coordinate with your partner to recruit Soldati, expand your influence, and seize control of Mandamenti (districts) through tactical planning and calculated attacks. Success depends on perfect timing and synergy within your team. Goal of the Game: A team that controls at least 6 Mandamenti, or has one player controlling 5 Mandamenti, wins the game. Otherwise the winner is the team that controls the most Mandamenti after the 4th round. Game Flow The game lasts for a maximum of 4 rounds , each divided into two main phases: 1. Planning Phase Players take turns placing their family markers on the action board to prepare their orders. Placing Markers: Choose an action and place your marker on the field. If markers are already present, they are stacked; actions are later resolved from top to bottom. Actions: Recruit: Bring new Soldati from your supply into your headquarters or controlled areas. Move: Shift Soldati from one area to an adjacent one to establish presence or initiate attacks. Upgrade: Improve abilities on your family board (e.g., weapon strength or income). Income: Receive money (Lire) to pay for expensive actions and equipment. Secret Orders: Prepare special attack or defense plans that remain hidden until the Execution Phase. 2. Execution Phase The placed markers are resolved stack by stack, starting from the top. Execute Order: The player whose marker is on top performs the action. Combat: Conflict occurs whenever Soldati from opposing families meet in the same area. Resolution: Combat strength (Soldati + bonuses) is combined with secretly played combat plans. Consequence: The losing side must remove Soldati from the board; ties are often broken by the resources invested. Scoring At the end of the 4th round, a final scoring takes place if no team has achieved an automatic victory (5 Mandamenti): Controlled Areas: Each occupied territory grants points. Mandamenti: A team receives bonus points for each Mandamento (a group of 3 areas) where they hold the majority. Board Progress: Fully upgraded family abilities provide additional victory points. Variants and Options 2-Player Mode: Each player controls a full team of two families. 3-Player Mode: A neutral family acts as a buffer or is integrated into the conflict via specific rules. Optional Rule Changes: Adjustments to mobility or combat plans can be used to alter the game's dynamics.

community_text:
[Rating: 1/10] If they had treated this theme more respectfully, and made this into say, a historical simulation, I could accept that (for example: The Troubles: Shadow War in Northern Ireland 1964-1998).  But this is very distasteful.  I assume this will have little to no sales in Italy or perhaps be banned outright, similar to what Germany might do with certain WW2 themed things.

[Rating: 1/10] If you are behind, your actions are always to slow. Then you can look the next 2h how you get crushed.

[Rating: 1/10] mafia kills people, why the author didn't make the game in Nazi Germany with factions struggling to control the country or about the Rote Armee Fraktion terrorist kills in Germany? Shame on this. Mafia KILLS people.

[Rating: 1.5/10] I think the theme applied to this game is a blatant display of disrespect to Italy and italians.

[Rating: 2/10] Not my kind of game. Don’t like area control, bluffing and team play. Don’t like the theme either.   The worker placement part felt very fresh and clever.

[Rating: 2/10] Vom Szenario sehr interessant. Aber Umsetzung mäh. Zu zäh, kompliziert, umständlich und zu imba. Einmal im Hintertreffen, dann Goodbye. Der Startspieler hat zu Beginn viel zu große Vorteile. Den dann "wegzukaufen" ist auch viel zu teuer. Einmal gespielt und nie wieder. War für mich die reinste Zeitverschwendung.

[Rating: 3/10] It has some imteresting mechanics but it in the end it is overly long for what is it. It could be a lot more streamlined in many places. The combat mechanic is the worst part of the game and ultimately the deciding factor why I will steer away from this game in the future.   The combat card choosing mechanic turns the game into a 50-50 odds situation and the game is ultimately decided by those ridiculous double guessing 50-50 battles. [Rating: 3/10] Great theme and components. The action selection is interesting but in service of what felt like a mediocre game. It actually took me a few hours to emerge from the doldrums the game put me in ?

[Rating: 3/10] This might be a decent game but the theme immediately turns me off of this one.  It's also not really my type of game but I do play a game from time to time that friends who play the games I want to try wish to try - but no, this one isn't going to see another play for me:)

[Rating: 3/10] Horrible. 1h rules teach. Retarded iconography. Complicated for no reason. Why anyone would play games like this when El Grande exists is beyond me. I’m not in the same hobby as these people. Never again.

[Rating: 3.5/10] Imho, it's pretty horribly balanced. I could almost tell from the start my family sucked and wasn't surprised to find I had guessed right which family was going to dominate our game.

[Rating: 4/10] Over long GoT clone, with nice clean art and graphic design, but a game from the 'throw everything into the pot' school of design that is popular at the moment, but doesn't interest me in the least.  I could happily lose the first and last round.  I also suspect (after about 8 hours of playing it), that the assymetry causes balance issues. I did not love it.
